issues.detail: Error handling is thin: it does not cover troubleshooting for hooks not firing (for example a missing executable bit or a non-Node/GUI Git client), ESM vs CJS config loading failures, shallow-clone CI failures when the base SHA is unavailable, or pushes to a branch with no pull_request event.

scenarios.name: husky-commit-msg-hook-setup
scenarios.rationale: B covers every rubric item: the install, `husky init`, the exact commit-msg line, an extends-conventional config, the `prepare` script for teammates, and the `npm test` pre-commit note with a fix; A removes `.husky/pre-commit` rather than editing it and never says `husky init` adds the prepare script (it sets it manually), and A also hasn't executed anything.

scenarios.name: restrict-scopes-and-header-length
scenarios.rationale: Both configs match the rubric exactly and show a failing `feat(mobile)` commit with a `scope-enum` error and a passing `fix(api)`-style commit; B edges ahead by showing fuller error output, a scope-case failure and a note on scope-empty, though A adds CI notes and more husky detail.

scenarios.name: ci-lint-pr-commits
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: pull_request trigger, fetch-depth 0, Node 22, `npm ci`, the exact commitlint command, CI as the enforcement point, and linting the PR title for squash-merge. A uses `npm install --no-save` instead of `npm ci` and says it couldn't write the files, though its guidance is otherwise solid.
